title: Burst Capacity Dashboards Spec (Dedicated Burst Pools)
author: Sergio Costa
body:
## Overview
This page specifies the internal (Redwood-only) dashboards required to operate and safely roll out the Dedicated “Burst Capacity” option. The dashboards are intended to support:
- Per-tenant transparency (what is bursting, where, and why it was denied)
- Pool health monitoring (saturation, errors, throttles, circuit breaker behavior)
- Neighbor protection validation (tail latency/throughput regressions on baseline Dedicated and Hosted fleets)
- Fast incident triage and forensics (correlate admits/denies, routing decisions, fleet capacity signals)

This spec covers:
- Dashboard taxonomy and required panels
- Metric and label conventions (including cardinality constraints)
- Drill-down flows and links to runbooks
- Baseline alert hooks (actual alert rules are defined in the observability-pack repo)

Non-goals:
- Customer-facing dashboards (Console views are tracked separately)
- Full billing reconciliation views (shadow metering reports are tracked under billing hooks)

## Audience
- SRE on-call (primary)
- Platform + Routing engineers (secondary)
- Fleet capacity team (secondary)
- Product/CS during pilot (read-only)

## Definitions
- Baseline Dedicated capacity: reserved tenant pool capacity with dedicated guarantees.
- Burst pool: controlled shared pool that Dedicated tenants may temporarily draw from subject to admission policy.
- Admission decision: policy outcome for a request to use burst capacity (allow/deny + reason).
- Neighbor SLO: “do no harm” protection for other tenants and for the hosted fleet.

## Data sources
- Metrics: Prometheus (via Mimir) + Grafana
- Logs: Loki (structured logs from routing + policy service)
- Traces: Tempo (sampling enabled; exemplars from key histograms)
- Fleet capacity signals: fleet-telemetry ingestion (exported as Prometheus gauges)

## Metric naming and label conventions
### Required metrics (canonical names)
The following names are the canonical names used in dashboard queries. If upstream services currently emit different names, the dashboard should use recording rules to normalize.

1) Admission and policy
- redwood_burst_admission_requests_total{result="allowed|denied", deny_reason="...", region="...", pool="..."}
- redwood_burst_policy_eval_latency_ms_bucket{region="..."}
- redwood_burst_circuit_breaker_state{region="...", pool="..."}  (0/1)
- redwood_burst_cooldown_active{tenant_scope="...", tenant_hash="...", region="..."} (0/1)

2) Usage and traffic
- redwood_burst_requests_total{tenant_hash="...", region="...", pool="...", model_family="..."}
- redwood_burst_tokens_total{tenant_hash="...", region="...", pool="...", model_family="..."}
- redwood_dedicated_requests_total{tenant_hash="...", region="...", model_family="..."}
- redwood_dedicated_tokens_total{tenant_hash="...", region="...", model_family="..."}

3) Pool capacity / saturation
- redwood_burst_pool_capacity_gpus{region="...", pool="...", gpu_type="..."}
- redwood_burst_pool_allocated_gpus{region="...", pool="...", gpu_type="..."}
- redwood_burst_pool_inflight_requests{region="...", pool="..."}
- redwood_burst_pool_queue_depth{region="...", pool="..."}
- redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio{region="...", pool="..."}  (0.0–1.0)

4) Latency / quality of service
- redwood_inference_request_latency_ms_bucket{fleet="dedicated|burst|hosted", region="...", model_family="..."}
- redwood_inference_time_to_first_token_ms_bucket{fleet="dedicated|burst|hosted", region="...", model_family="..."}
- redwood_inference_generation_tokens_per_second_bucket{fleet="dedicated|burst", region="...", model_family="..."}

5) Errors / rejects / load shedding
- redwood_requests_rejected_total{fleet="dedicated|burst", reason="rate_limit|admission_denied|pool_saturated|circuit_open|quota", region="..."}
- redwood_http_responses_total{service="routing", status_code="...", region="..."}

### Label policy (cardinality constraints)
We explicitly avoid high-cardinality blow-ups in Grafana and the metrics backend.
- tenant identifiers MUST use tenant_hash (stable, non-reversible hash). Do not use tenant_id or tenant_name in metrics labels.
- model identifier MUST use model_family (e.g., llama-3, qwen2, mistral) rather than full model_version.
- pool MUST use a small taxonomy value (e.g., burst-a10g-usw2-1). Avoid instance/cluster identifiers.
- Optional: for deep dives, use logs/traces for raw tenant_id and request_id.

Approved label set by metric type:
- Counters: {region, pool, result/deny_reason, tenant_hash (only on usage counters), model_family (only where useful)}
- Histograms: {fleet, region, model_family}
- Capacity gauges: {region, pool, gpu_type}

## Dashboard taxonomy
We will ship 4 Grafana dashboards under the folder:
"Platform / Dedicated / Burst Capacity"

Table: Dashboards and owners
| Dashboard | Primary purpose | Default viewers | DRI |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Burst Overview (Global) | “Is burst healthy right now?” across regions/pools | SRE on-call | Sergio Costa |
| 2. Burst Pools (Per Region/Pool) | Pool saturation, capacity, error modes, circuit breaker | SRE + Fleet | Vanessa Ortiz (data), Sergio Costa (dash) |
| 3. Burst Admission (Policy + Routing) | Admit/deny trends, reasons, policy latency, cooldown behavior | Platform + Routing + SRE | Jordan Lee (data), Mina Haddad (data), Sergio Costa (dash) |
| 4. Tenant Burst Drilldown | Per-tenant burst usage, denies, latency, impact vs baseline | SRE + CS (pilot) | Logan Wright (data), Sergio Costa (dash) |

Each dashboard MUST:
- Provide time range presets: 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d
- Provide variables: region, pool, model_family (where relevant), tenant_hash (tenant drilldown only)
- Link to the saturation runbook and the admission SLO page

## Dashboard 1: Burst Overview (Global)
### Goal
Single-pane “health and risk” view to support on-call: do we have saturation, elevated deny rates, latency regressions, or circuit breaker openings?

### Variables
- $region (multi-select, default all)
- $pool (multi-select, default all)

### Required panels (in order)
1) Executive summary (stat row)
- Burst admission allow rate (last 15m)
- Burst deny rate (last 15m)
- Pools above 0.85 saturation (count)
- Circuit breakers open (count)
- Dedicated baseline p99 drift vs 24h median (per region)

2) Admission allow/deny over time
- Query: rate(redwood_burst_admission_requests_total{result=~"allowed|denied"}[5m]) by (region)
- Overlay deny_reason breakdown (stacked) for denied

3) Top deny reasons (last 1h)
- Stacked bar or table: sum(increase(redwood_burst_admission_requests_total{result="denied"}[1h])) by (deny_reason)
- Expected top reasons: pool_saturated, tenant_limit, cooldown_active, circuit_open, region_ineligible

4) Pool saturation heatmap
- Heatmap: max_over_time(redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio[5m]) by (region, pool)
- Threshold coloring: 0.70 (yellow), 0.85 (orange), 0.95 (red)

5) Tail latency impact (neighbor protection)
- Dedicated p99 latency by region: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_latency_ms_bucket{fleet="dedicated"}[5m])) by (le, region))
- Hosted p99 latency by region: same with fleet="hosted"
- Annotation: times when circuit breaker state == 1 (open)

6) Error/reject signals
- 429 and 503 rates from routing service
- Rejected requests by reason (admission_denied vs pool_saturated vs quota)

### Links
- “Burst Pool Saturation Runbook” (eng-sre/runbooks)
- “Burst Admission SLOs & Alerts” (eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets)

## Dashboard 2: Burst Pools (Per Region/Pool)
### Goal
Deep operational view for a specific pool: capacity, demand, queueing, errors, and effectiveness of protections (cooldown/circuit breaker).

### Variables
- $region (single-select, required)
- $pool (single-select, required)
- $gpu_type (optional, default all)

### Required panels
1) Pool status summary
- Saturation ratio (current + 1h sparkline)
- Capacity GPUs vs allocated GPUs
- Circuit breaker state (0/1) + transitions (last 24h)

2) Capacity and allocation
- redwood_burst_pool_capacity_gpus vs redwood_burst_pool_allocated_gpus by gpu_type
- Notes panel: expected warm capacity and constraints (link to fleet topology page)

3) Inflight and queue depth
- redwood_burst_pool_inflight_requests
- redwood_burst_pool_queue_depth
- Alert hint: queue depth > 0 for sustained 10m is usually a leading indicator of tail latency regression.

4) Burst throughput
- Burst requests/sec and tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Optional: tokens/sec distribution if available (p50/p95)

5) Latency for burst fleet (pool-specific proxy)
- Use fleet="burst" latency histograms at region level; filter by model_family if needed
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) p95/p99

6) Error and load shedding
- redwood_requests_rejected_total{fleet="burst"} by reason
- HTTP 5xx rate from routing for routes targeting $pool

7) Top tenants consuming burst (bounded cardinality)
- Table: top 20 tenant_hash by burst_tokens_total over 1h (requires tenant_hash label on usage metric)
- IMPORTANT: Do not display tenant names; provide a “lookup” link to an internal tool/log query.

### Drilldowns
- Click tenant_hash -> opens Dashboard 4 (Tenant Burst Drilldown) with tenant_hash set
- Click “circuit open” annotation -> opens logs panel query (routing + policy service)

## Dashboard 3: Burst Admission (Policy + Routing)
### Goal
Validate admission policy behavior and determinism; detect regressions (e.g., sudden deny spike due to config/cache issues) and confirm that routing fallback semantics behave as designed.

### Variables
- $region (multi-select)
- $pool (multi-select)

### Required panels
1) Policy eval latency
- p50/p95/p99 of redwood_burst_policy_eval_latency_ms
- SLO guidance: p99 < 50ms over 10m window (see SLO page)

2) Admission decisions over time
- Allowed vs denied, stacked by region
- Overlay total request rate to distinguish traffic drops from policy behavior changes

3) Deny reasons over time
- Stacked series for deny_reason
- Explicitly highlight: cooldown_active, circuit_open, pool_saturated, tenant_limit

4) Cooldown behavior
- Count of tenants in cooldown (sum of redwood_burst_cooldown_active) by region
- Rate of cooldown activations (if emitted as events counter)

5) Circuit breaker behavior
- redwood_burst_circuit_breaker_state transitions by pool
- Correlate with saturation ratio and p99 latency drift

6) Routing fallback outcomes
- If available, chart: baseline_success vs burst_success vs fallback_model vs fallback_region vs hard_fail
- Metric suggestion (if not already emitted): redwood_routing_route_outcome_total{outcome="baseline|burst|fallback|deny", reason="..."}

### Built-in debug panels (collapsed by default)
- “Recent config change events” (from audit logs; Loki query)
- “Policy cache hit rate” (if available)

## Dashboard 4: Tenant Burst Drilldown
### Goal
Support pilot operations and escalations: for a single tenant, show burst usage, denies, and performance compared to baseline. This dashboard is used during customer escalations and post-incident forensics.

### Variables
- $tenant_hash (single-select, required)
- $region (multi-select, default all)
- $model_family (multi-select, default all)

### Required panels
1) Tenant usage summary
- Burst tokens (1h, 24h)
- Burst requests (1h, 24h)
- Burst share: burst_tokens / (burst_tokens + dedicated_tokens)

2) Admission denies for tenant
- Denies over time and breakdown by deny_reason
- Table: “Top regions/pools where denies occurred”

3) Tenant latency comparison
- Dedicated fleet p95/p99 for tenant’s traffic (if tenant-level latency is not available as metrics, show region/model_family level and provide trace/log link)
- Burst fleet p95/p99
- TTFT p95/p99

4) Spillover / neighbor protection indicators
- Region-level dedicated p99 drift during tenant’s burst activity (context)
- Hosted p99 drift (context)

5) Request samples (traces)
- Link panel to Tempo search using exemplar trace IDs from latency histograms (where available)
- Loki log query template filtered by tenant_hash and “burst_admission” fields

### Access notes
This dashboard is internal. During pilot, CS can be granted read-only access to this dashboard folder; do not export screenshots containing tenant-identifying info.

## Standard annotations (all dashboards)
Dashboards should include annotations for:
- Feature flag toggles (burst enabled/disabled per tenant or region)
- Circuit breaker open/close events
- Fleet pool capacity changes (planned or automated)

Source for annotations:
- Loki: routing audit logs and burst policy audit logs
- Optional: a lightweight "events" metric exported as annotations (preferred if available)

## Alert hooks (what the dashboards must make easy to validate)
Alert definitions live in the observability-pack repo, but dashboards must contain panels that mirror alert conditions so on-call can rapidly confirm/deny.

Minimum alert conditions to support:
- Pool saturation ratio > 0.95 for 5m (by region/pool)
- Burst deny rate > 20% for 10m (global and per-region)
- Dedicated baseline p99 latency regression > 15% vs 24h median for 10m (per region)
- Circuit breaker open > 15m (by region/pool)
- Policy eval p99 latency > 50ms for 10m

## Runbook integration
Every dashboard must include a “Next steps” text panel with:
- Link: Runbook – Burst Pool Saturation
- Quick checks:
  1) Is the circuit breaker open?
  2) Is saturation sustained or spiky?
  3) Are denies predominantly pool_saturated vs tenant_limit/cooldown?
  4) Is dedicated or hosted p99 drifting?
- Escalation pointers:
  - Fleet on-call for capacity shortfall / pool anomalies
  - Routing on-call for fallback/deny semantics regressions
  - Platform on-call for policy/cache/config regressions

## Implementation notes (Grafana)
- Folder: Platform / Dedicated / Burst Capacity
- Use recording rules where possible to reduce expensive queries (especially histograms).
- Tables showing “Top tenants” must be limited (Top 20) and use increase() over a bounded window (1h/6h).
- Prefer 5m rates for counters; avoid 30s unless necessary.
- Use consistent thresholds and units across dashboards (ms, tokens/sec, ratio).

## Open questions / follow-ups
1) Do we have tenant-scoped latency histograms (safe cardinality) or do we rely on traces/logs for per-tenant latency? (DRI: Logan Wright)
2) Are routing fallback outcomes emitted as a dedicated metric? If not, add to routing instrumentation plan. (DRI: Mina Haddad)
3) Confirm which pool taxonomy string is stable across regions and deployments (avoid renaming churn in dashboards). (DRI: Vanessa Ortiz)

## Change log
- 2025-06-24: Initial draft created (taxonomy + required panels).
- 2025-07-06: Added neighbor protection panels (dedicated/hosted p99 drift) and deny reason breakdown standards.
- 2025-07-18: Updated label policy to require tenant_hash only; clarified top-tenant tables and drilldown links.
